steps.message:
Diagnosis confirmed. Let me explain the root cause before patching:

**Root cause** (`DocumentIO.saveDocument`): the decision to write to disk is based on comparing the editor text against a *history snapshot* (`document.getInitialVersion().getContent()`) instead of the actual file state.

For a new note, undo/redo history is disabled by default, so `DocumentEditFragment.loadDocument()`'s `addToHistory()` is a no-op and the history stays **empty**. `saveDocument()` then does `setDoHistory(true)` followed by `setFile(...)`, which snapshots the document *as it is at save time*. If the user waited ≥ `HISTORY_DELTA` (5 s) — which is exactly when the save icon becomes enabled — the typed text has already been pushed into `_document`, so that first snapshot already contains it. Hence `currentText.equals(documentInitial.getContent())` is `true`, the write is **skipped**, and `saveDocument()` still reports success. Every later save (back press / `onPause`) hits the same condition, so the file is never created. Skipping the wait leaves the snapshot empty, which is why that path works.

Done. `./gradlew clean assembleDebug` → **BUILD SUCCESSFUL**, and the full unit test suite passes.

## Root cause

`DocumentIO.saveDocument()` decided whether to touch the disk by comparing the editor text against a **history snapshot** instead of the actual file:

```java
if (!currentText.equals(documentInitial.getContent())) { ...write... } else { ret = true; }
```

For a new note, undo/redo history is disabled by default (`isEditorHistoryEnabled()` → `false`), so `DocumentEditFragment.loadDocument()`'s `addToHistory()` is a no-op and the history stays **empty**. Then inside `saveDocument()`:

1. `document.setDoHistory(true)` re-enables history,
2. `document.setFile(<title>.md)` triggers `addToHistory()`, which snapshots the document **as it is right now**,
3. `getInitialVersion()` returns that snapshot as `_history.get(0)`.

If the user waited ≥ `HISTORY_DELTA` (5 s) — precisely when the save icon becomes enabled — the delayed `_document.setContent(text)` had already pushed the typed text into the model, so that first snapshot *already contains the typed text*. The comparison is therefore equal, the write is skipped, and `saveDocument()` still returns `true`. The back press (`onPause` → `saveDocument()`) hits the same condition, so **the file is never created**. Skipping the wait leaves the snapshot empty, which is exactly why that path worked.

## Fix

1. **`DocumentIO.saveDocument()`** — base the write decision on the real filesystem state: write if the target file doesn't exist, or if its on-disk content differs from the editor text. This also fixes the related silent-data-loss case where editing content back to an earlier history state was never persisted.
2. **`DocumentEditFragment.saveDocument()`** — after a save, sync the fragment arguments to the now-real file (`EXTRA_PATH` + `EXTRA_PATH_IS_FOLDER=false`). Previously the arguments still said "this is a folder", so any `onResume()` → `checkReloadDisk()` would build a brand-new empty document with a fresh random filename and discard the note just written.

## Verification

Added `app/src/test/java/net/gsantner/markor/util/DocumentIoSaveRepoTest.java` replicating the reported steps plus regression guards. Against the **unpatched** code the repro test fails exactly at the reported symptom:

```
pressingSaveThenBackCreatesTheNote FAILED
  [note file created on save] expected:<true> but was:<false>
```

With the fix, all four tests pass: save creates the note, back-without-save still works, renaming an existing note preserves content and removes the old file, and reverting content is persisted.
